images.title: Reading the rice and wheat scale
images.purpose: Shows the colour scale from −100 to +100 and what a value on it means.
images.composition: One long, thick horizontal colour bar across the middle of the frame, with end and centre numbers below and two marker pins above. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A long horizontal bar, about two thirds of the frame wide, filled flat in three equal parts with no gradient: the left third amber (#E69F00), the middle third white with a thin outline, the right third teal (#0072B2). Below the bar, three numbers: '−100' at the left end, '0' at the centre, '+100' at the right end. Under the left end the words 'more wheat'; under the right end the words 'more rice'. Above the bar, two reddish purple (#CC79A7) pins: one at 78 percent of the way from the centre to the left end, labelled 'Punjab −78', and one at the centre, labelled 'Bihar about 0'. Exactly 1 bar and 2 pins.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Positive means rice is preferred, negative means wheat, near zero means balanced.
images.description: Shows the colour scale from −100 to +100 and what a value on it means.
images.context: +100 means the largest rice over wheat gap, not that no wheat is eaten.

image_decisions.why: The scale is the key to the whole infographic; one clean bar with two readings shows how to use it.
